name: Mirusavis
sum: Enantiornithean from the Yixian Formation of China, a female preserved during her egg-laying cycle.
holotype: A partial subadult skeleton, the only specimen (number in Wang et al. 2020).
biology: Medullary bone shows the female was in her laying cycle when she died.
author: Wang et al. 2020

images.artist: Min Wang, Jingmai K. O’Connor, Alida M. Bailleul & Zhiheng Li
images.caption: Mirusavis parvus (Wikimedia Commons; kind assigned from the file name, not yet checked on the triage page).

sources.text: Wang, Min; O’Connor, Jingmai K.; Bailleul, Alida M.; Li, Zhiheng 1 Ju. Evolution and distribution of medullary bone: evidence from a new Early Cretaceous enantiornithine bird. National Science Review 7(6): 1068–1078. doi:10.1093/nsr/nwz214
